rationale: Item asks how the PATCO firings fit an argument about a 20-year union decline shown in a chart. Key answer qualifies the claim (catalytic within a broader structural decline, not the sole engine), which is textbook 3.D: explaining how evidence supports/modifies an argument. Topic is Reagan-era labor politics, 1981.

Item asks which criticism of Reaganomics is best supported by the chart plus the review's own account. Judging which claim the evidence supports/modifies is 3.D work. Topic is supply-side Reaganomics and the 1980s deficit under Reagan.

Item asks the test-taker to identify the historical development the data show (manufacturing employment share falling 25% to 10% from 1970 to 2010) = 1.A identify a historical concept/development/process. Content is the post-1970s restructuring of the American economy.

Item presents a student's claim (output fell by more than half) and asks which correction the chart requires. Correcting a claim by showing what the evidence actually measures is 3.D (how claims/evidence support or refute an argument). Content is deindustrialization and the changing economy.

Item asks which service sectors absorbed displaced factory workers (retail, finance, health care) = identifying a historical process, 1.A. Content is the shift from manufacturing to service employment in the late 20th century.

Item asks what the Spanish mission system best illustrates (conversion + extending Spanish control) = identifying a historical concept/process from visual evidence, 1.A. Missions as a site of cultural contact/conversion fit 1.6 'Cultural Interactions Between Europeans, Native Americans, and Africans' better than 1.5 (labor/slavery/caste), though the key's 'extending control' language makes this a medium-confidence call.

Item asks what the Indian Reorganization Act of 1934 did relative to earlier policy (replaced forced assimilation with tribal self-government) = identifying a historical development/process, 1.A. The IRA is a New Deal-era policy, so 7.10 'The New Deal' is the best official topic. FLAG: the item's period field is 'U6' but 1934 is Period 7 (1890-1945); no U6 topic fits, so the period appears mislabeled.

Item asks what the completion of the Erie Canal most directly did (made NYC the commercial capital) = identifying a historical development, 1.A. The canal is Market Revolution internal-improvements content, best fit 4.5 'Market Revolution: Industrialization'.
Item asks which American action the domino theory most directly shaped (Vietnam escalation) = identifying a historical development, 1.A. Directly a Vietnam War item, 8.8.

Item presents a Thoreau excerpt and asks what claim/method the passage describes (civil disobedience) = 3.A, identifying a claim/argument in a text-based source. The poll-tax protest against the Mexican War puts the best official topic at 5.3 'The Mexican-American War' (medium confidence, since the stem foregrounds the protest concept rather than the war itself).
Item asks what purpose Parliament itself stated in the Sugar Act preamble (raise revenue) = 2.A, identifying a source's purpose from the text. Clearly 3.3 'Taxation Without Representation'.

Item asks what the Middle Passage horrors contributed most directly to in the early 1800s (the 1808 federal ban on importation) = identifying a historical development/process, 1.A. FLAG: the item's period field is 'U2', but the tested outcome (the 1808 importation ban) is Period 4; no U2 topic fits. Best official topic is 4.12 'African Americans in the Early Republic'; the period appears mislabeled (should be U4).

Item asks which options show continuity with the early-republic non-entanglement preference except NATO = identifying patterns/connections among developments, 5.A. Early-republic foreign policy/neutrality fits 4.4 'America on the World Stage'.

Item asks what inspired the 1830s-40s reform wave (a religious revival preaching human perfectibility) = identifying the historical context for a development, 4.A. Directly the Second Great Awakening, 4.10.

Item asks what the early-1900s conservation movement led most directly to (growth of national parks, forests, wildlife refuges) = identifying a historical development, 1.A. Conservation is a Progressive-era reform, best fit 7.4 'The Progressives'.
